title: Borealis inference health & cost alignment sync
summary: Quarterly health/check-in focused on usage spike in Feb, unexpected cost increase tied to late-token growth, discussion of latency tail on hosted endpoints, verification of SOC2/KMS posture for upcoming pilot expansion, agree to run a focused performance benchmark and an optimization rightsize proposal.
topics: usage trends and cost spike analysis
next quarter roadmap and pilot expansion
action_items: Luis Ortega - run token-level trace and share CSV with p95/p99 slices (due 2026-03-25)
Maya Chen - share detailed cost breakdown and proposed rightsize options (due 2026-03-23)
Derek Kim - provide current infra cost center tags and expected scaling window (due 2026-03-22)
Amira Nasser - confirm which KMS/HSM provider they must use and send access requirements (due 2026-03-26)
next_steps: Schedule 60m technical deep dive (SE-led) to run benchmark against their prod-like traces
Pilot proposal for Dedicated capacity with 30-day canary and cost SLOs
Send SOC2 and network architecture docs; follow-up security questionnaire
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-19 15:00 PDT; duration 52m; attendees Maya, Luis (Redwood); Ravi, Sofia, Derek, Amira (Borealis)

00:00 Maya: ok everyone thanks for joining, I think we have the usual agenda, quick usage review, cost anomaly, then tech follow-up. is the timing still ok for folks?
00:14 Ravi: yeah this works, we wanted to get ahead of the spike we saw in feb, seemed higher than forecast.
00:29 Sofia: and the p99 latency popped a couple times during peak, users reported sluggish responses.
00:45 Luis: got it, we pulled some preliminary metrics, looks like the late token counts increased for a small subset of prompts, could be prompt changes or a model roll.
00:59 Derek: we didn't roll anything on our side; our orchestrator kept the same request patterns.
01:12 Maya: ok so first hypothesis is prompt drift -> longer output -> more tokens -> cost. second hypothesis is model variant change, maybe quantization or new checkpoint.
01:30 Ravi: we did change a system prompt in prod on feb 9, it added a contextual history dump for debugging, that might be it, though we thought it was temporary.
01:45 Amira: quick security note, before any dedicated pilot we need confirmation on KMS integration and audit logs availability, SOC 2 proof would be helpful.
02:01 Maya: absolutely, we'll share our SOC2 cert and the audit log doc. Luis, can you add a note about audit log retention?
02:12 Luis: yes i'll include retention windows and log schema.
02:20 Sofia: on the latency p99, is that something Redwood can help with via batching or KV cache on the inference side?
02:36 Luis: yes, we have prefix KV caching that can cut repeated token generation, and continuous batching helps if you can tolerate a small additional ms of queuing. but that trades off with tail latency.
02:51 Derek: what about dedicated vs hosted — if we move to Dedicated does that fix the tail?
03:03 Maya: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor and gives predictable throughput; it doesn't eliminate p99 spikes from long-token requests, but combined with autoscaling and cache rules it can improve tail behavior.
03:18 Ravi: cost is the big blocker — Dedicated is more committed spend, we need ROI numbers.
03:25 Maya: understood, we'll run a rightsize analysis and show expected unit cost per 1k tokens vs hosted mixed profile.
03:38 Sofia: can you also show effects of quantization on cost and quality? we tried a 4-bit profile internally but saw hallucination uptick.
03:50 Luis: yep we can show quant profiles, but quality regressions depend on prompt sets; we'll recommend a lab of 50 golden prompts to evaluate.
04:07 Ravi: sounds good. also, the feb spike coincided with increased long form summarization requests from marketing, maybe multi-doc prompts.
04:20 Maya: okay we'll ask for a sample trace of those marketing requests — if you can export anonymized request examples that helps.
04:35 Derek: we can provide request traces, but need to strip PII; is Redwood able to accept sanitized traces via S3?
04:46 Maya: yes S3 or secure upload, we'll provide a presigned link.
04:54 Amira: security — what about network connectivity for Private deployment? we have an internal policy preferring VPC peering over open endpoints.
05:06 Luis: our Private offering supports VPC peering and customer-managed control plane; we can detail the network flows in a diagram.
05:18 Amira: please include required firewall rules and ports.
05:24 Maya: will do. shifting back to cost, do you have any internal chargeback tags we should map?
05:33 Derek: yes we tag by product line and environment, we'll share the tags.
05:40 Maya: perfect. next i wanted to surface a usage anomaly: your top 10 prompts account for 47% of tokens and one prompt in particular had a median length 3x typical.
05:54 Ravi: that matches the marketing long-form; do you have more granular breakdown by user bucket?
06:05 Luis: we can slice by api_key and route, i'll include p95/p99 by route.
06:15 Sofia: what's the recommended mitigation while we analyze? rate limits, shortening context, or rewrites?
06:23 Maya: short term: enforce route-level token caps + request throttling. medium term: optimize prompt and enable KV cache + batching.
06:33 Ravi: ok, can you propose caps and expected impact on latency and error rate?
06:41 Luis: yes we'll model expected token reduction and show simulated latency curves.
06:49 Maya: anything else on reliability?
06:53 Derek: we saw a couple 503s during high traffic windows last month, are those retriable?
07:02 Luis: 503s in hosted can be retried; sometimes they're from burst throttling. Dedicated with burst capacity reduces those occurrences.
07:15 Ravi: will a canary Dedicated deployment be possible for a single product line?
07:22 Maya: yes that's a common pattern: Dedicated for say marketing route, hosted for the rest, with automatic fallback on capacity rules.
07:35 Sofia: timeline — if we decide to pilot, how long to stand up Dedicated?
07:41 Maya: typically 2-3 weeks for provisioning and model onboarding plus a 1-week canary.
07:49 Amira: on compliance, i need to confirm encryption at rest keys — who manages KMS?
07:56 Maya: supported options: Redwood-managed KMS or customer KMS (bring-your-own) via AWS KMS/Azure Key Vault; for Private we support HSM integrations.
08:09 Amira: ok we'll check internal policy.
08:15 Ravi: quick question about evals and quality monitoring — do you have regression alerts tied to prompt sets?
08:23 Luis: yes Redwood Optimize can watch golden prompts and alert on quality degradation and token cost regressions.
08:31 Sofia: can Optimize run as a scheduled job against our test set?
08:36 Luis: yes we can configure daily/weekly runs and alert thresholds.
08:42 Maya: next — pricing. we'll send a proposed pilot quote and cost projection, and also a side-by-side of hosted vs Dedicated.
08:51 Ravi: great. also please list assumptions around throughput, avg tokens, and retention.
08:58 Maya: will do.
09:02 (silence for a bit as folks skim shared doc)
09:20 Derek: one more infra note, we need to maintain our internal tag mapping for chargebacks, if Dedicated can be charged to our cost centers then that's preferable.
09:31 Maya: we'll map billing to tags in the proposal.
09:36 Amira: security follow-up - we need to see redwood's penetration test summary and third-party audit contacts.
09:45 Maya: i'll include the pentest summary and security contacts in the packet.
09:51 Ravi: ok to recap next steps?
09:55 Maya: yes i'll recap: Luis will run token/p99 traces and share csv; Maya will send cost breakdown, SOC2 and pentest summary; Derek will send tags and scaling window; Amira will confirm KMS constraint. and we'll schedule SE deep dive next week. anyone want to adjust?
10:19 Sofia: that covers it. thanks Maya.
10:23 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the deep dive and links for trace upload.
10:30 (meeting ends)
